formula: vFA ~ PCL + Coors + Age + (PCL | ID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro, 08-Introduction-to-Multilevel-Models.Rmd at b04814b5), open-ended exercise 3 Project 5183: game logs of 7 Rockies starting pitchers (ID) who started games before and after the 75-pitch limit of June 20, 2012 (PCL); key responses vFA, K.9 (the column K/9), ERA and Pitpct, PCL the primary covariate, Coors and Age confounders to control. The book fits no model but warns of variance components at 0 and correlations at 1, so the pitcher-level PCL slope is proposed. Responses in page order: rows 2 and 3 are K/9 and ERA, the fourth, Pitpct, is ignored. The other game statistics are game outcomes or the parts of the responses (SO, ER, IP, Str, Pit), ignored; Opp (opponent) and Team are no documented factor.

formula: `K/9` ~ PCL + Coors + Age + (PCL | ID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 exercise Project 5183, the second key response (strikeouts per nine innings, K.9 in the book); design and proposed model as row 1.

formula: ERA ~ PCL + Coors + Age + (PCL | ID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 exercise Project 5183, the third key response (earned runs per nine innings); design and proposed model as row 1.

formula: cbind(made, shots - made) ~ ball + order + distance + (1 | id)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: the file is in the book repository at b04814b5 but no chapter, exercise or README loads or describes it (searched all Rmd files and the web). Each id shoots twice, once with a tennis and once with a ping-pong ball (ball) in a counterbalanced order (order), making made of shots throws from a distance set per shooting group; id is the grouping a reader would model, rendered as a random intercept. group (shooting group, nests the ids) and the shooter traits (year, basketball, height, hand, glasses, HSsports, awake, underhand, sleep) are left as unused columns.

formula: price ~ overall_satisfaction + reviews + room_type + accommodates + bedrooms + minstay + district + WalkScore + TransitScore + BikeScore + PctBlack + (1 | neighborhood)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro) open-ended exercise 2, Airbnb in Chicago (Trinh and Ameri 2018): 1561 listings merged with information on their neighborhood (1 of 43), asked to build a multilevel model for price with listing- and neighborhood-level traits; no model is fitted, the formula is proposed from the listed variables. district (1 of 9, Chicago's districts, a neighborhood-level classification) is a covariate. HighBlack is derived from PctBlack and not a column. Row 2 is the ch. 11 exercise on the same table.

formula: I(overall_satisfaction == 5) ~ price + reviews + room_type + accommodates + bedrooms + minstay + district + WalkScore + TransitScore + BikeScore + PctBlack + (1 | neighborhood)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 1, Airbnb in Chicago: satisfaction = 1 if overall_satisfaction is 5, else 0, modeled by a multilevel generalized model with listing and neighborhood traits; no model is fitted, the formula is proposed. RULE GAP: the documented response is the binary recode of overall_satisfaction, a half-star rating, so response_type records what the column holds (ordinal) while the formula keeps the source's binary recode.

formula: alcuse ~ I(age - 14) + coa + peer + peer:I(age - 14) + (I(age - 14) | id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 (ch-lon) guided exercise 1, Teen alcohol use (Curran et al. 1997, accessed via Singer and Willett 2003); the same table is the conceptual exercise of ch. 7. Model B is the unconditional growth model in age14 = age - 14 (random intercept and slope per id, the book's convention), Model C adds coa and peer to both level-two equations, and Model D removes coa from the slope equation, so D is written here; Singer and Willett ch. 4 fit the same model (their Model E, recalled, not reopened) on alcohol1_pp. male is an unused covariate. A copy of alcohol1_pp, which the registry holds under pymc_examples, rabe_hesketh and alda.

formula: ambiguity ~ incumbent + democrat + mismatch + abs(ideology) + distLean + attHeterogeneity + demHeterogeneity + (1 | distID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro) open-ended exercise 1, Political ambiguity: Chapp et al. (2019, Social Science Computer Review, Going Vague) fit a multilevel model for candidates' ambiguity scores with predictors at the candidate and the district level (distID), per the book; the paper was not read, so the formula is built from the hypotheses the book quotes (incumbency 1b, ideological distance mismatch 2a, ideological extremity as abs(ideology) 2b, attitudinal and demographic heterogeneity 3a and 3b) and the listed controls democrat and distLean. name is the candidate's label. Row 2 is the ch. 4 count response of the same table.

formula: totalIssuePages ~ ideology + democrat + (1 | distID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 4 (ch-poissonreg) guided exercise 7, Going vague: totalIssuePages, the number of issues a candidate comments on, modeled by a hurdle model with ideology and democrat in both parts (pscl hurdle, Poisson count part); the book fits no random effect, and the district intercept comes from the two-level structure ch. 8 documents for the same table. The formula names the count part; both parts take the same covariates.

formula: diverthours ~ year2013 + totalvisits1 + ems_basic + stations + ems_basic:year2013 + stations:year2013 + (year2013 | id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 (ch-lon) guided exercise 2, Ambulance diversions (Radtke et al. 2019): California hospitals (id) over 2013-2015, diverthours the response; the exercise's R code states Models D, D0, E and G by lmer, and Model G, the richest, is written here (D, D0 and E share its response and grouping). diverthours, hours of diversion status per year, is a duration, typed continuous as the source fits it by lmer. year, emslevel, totalvisits and admit duplicate year2013, ems_basic, totalvisits1 and admit1; admitrate and trauma_L0 are derived; divert and logdivert are alternate forms of the response. county (hospitals within counties) is no documented factor.

formula: foul.home ~ foul.diff + score.diff + lead.home + time + offensive + personal + foul.diff:offensive + foul.diff:personal + foul.diff:time + lead.home:time + (1 | game) + (1 | hometeam) + (1 | visitor)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM, 11-Generalized-Linear-Multilevel-Models.Rmd at b04814b5), case study on referee bias in college basketball: Model F (potential final model) glmer(foul.home ~ foul.diff + score.diff + lead.home + time + offensive + personal + foul.diff:offensive + foul.diff:personal + foul.diff:time + lead.home:time + (1|game) + (1|hometeam) + (1|visitor), family = binomial), crossed random intercepts for game, home team and visiting team. foul.vis is the complement of the response; foul.type is coded by the offensive, personal and shooting indicators, shooting the reference.

formula: removed ~ pvi2 + cperhs + cmedin + cperba + days2000 + obama + freqchal + sexexp + antifamily + occult + language + homosexuality + violence + (1 | state) + (1 | book)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 3, Book banning (Fast et al. 2011): challenges in U.S. states 2000-2010 without Texas, removed the primary response, predictors at the state level (pvi2, cperhs, cmedin, cperba), the book level (freqchal) and the challenge level; the page notes that a book can be challenged in several states and for several reasons, so state and book are crossed grouping factors. The page asks for multilevel models and fits none; the formula is proposed from the listed variables. booktitle labels book; author (books nest in authors) is no documented factor.

formula: rate ~ I(year - 2002) + instpct + instamt + faculty + tuition + faculty:I(year - 2002) + tuition:I(year - 2002) + (I(year - 2002) | id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 (ch-lon) open-ended exercise 2, Completion rates at U.S. colleges (IPEDS 2002-2009): rate the response, Level 1 predictors year, instpct and instamt, Level 2 predictors faculty and tuition, asked for multilevel models of baseline (2002) rates and their change to 2009; no model is fitted, so the growth model with the Level 2 predictors on intercept and slope is proposed in the book's two-level convention. instname labels id; state (institutions within states) is no documented factor.

formula: I(Vote == "1") ~ zfaminc + zmedinc + EconWorse + EducStatus + republican + EducStatus:republican + EconWorse:zfaminc + EconWorse:republican + (1 | inputstate)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 6 (ch-logreg) guided exercise 5, 2016 Election (CCES, Renier et al. 2018): model1a glm(Vote01 ~ zfaminc + zmedinc + EconWorse + EducStatus + republican + EducStatus:republican + EconWorse:zfaminc + EconWorse:republican, family = binomial), Vote01 = 1 for a Trump vote (Vote holds 1 or Other). The page plots one observation per state, carries state-level covariates (zmedinc, propforeign) and asks in part (h) whether the independence assumption holds, so voters are grouped by inputstate, rendered as a random intercept. Theory 2's immigration model (Noimmigrants) shares response and grouping and is not a row. faminc and medinc are the raw forms of zfaminc and zmedinc; inputstate_post repeats the state.

formula: mathn ~ female * sch_ses * dis_size + (female | dis_id:sch_id) + (1 | dis_id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 10 (ch-3level) guided exercise 2, Kentucky math scores (Bickel 2007): eighth graders in middle schools in districts, three levels. Model B adds female, nonwhite and their interaction at Level One; Model C drops the interaction and adds sch_ses to all Level Two equations; Model D drops nonwhite and adds dis_size to all Level Three equations, rerun with an error term only on the Level Three intercept, the version the exercise carries on with (3-way female, sch_ses, dis_size interaction); written here, the school-level female slope following the book's convention of an error term per Level Two equation. The exercise asks the reader to fit it and states no lmer call. A school code recurs across districts, so the school factor is dis_id:sch_id. readn is an alternate response, stud_nm the student id.

formula: Area ~ Species + Zone + Strata + Tree.height + Tree.girth + Branch.length + (1 | Species:Zone:Tree) + (1 | Branchnum)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 10 (ch-3level) open-ended exercise 2, Mudamalai leaf growth (Pray 2009): 5 trees from each of 3 species in each of 3 climate zones (Tree numbers 1-5 within zone, so a tree is Species:Zone:Tree), 3 branches from each of 3 strata per tree, 5 leaves per branch; leaf Area the response of interest, asked for a multilevel model and no model fitted, so the formula is proposed. Branchnum identifies a branch (Branch is its number within tree and stratum). Area was computed from Length and Width by regression for most leaves, so both are ignored. Herbivory, petiole sizes and Stomata (per stratum per tree) are left as unused columns.

formula: na ~ previous + I(audience == "Student(s)") + I(audience == "Juried Recital") + I(audience == "Public Performance") + I(perform_type == "Solo") + mpqpem + mpqab + I(instrument == "orchestral instrument") + mpqnem + mpqnem:I(perform_type == "Solo") + (previous + I(audience == "Student(s)") + I(audience == "Juried Recital") + I(audience == "Public Performance") + I(perform_type == "Solo") | id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro, 08-Introduction-to-Multilevel-Models.Rmd at b04814b5), section A Final Model for Music Performance Anxiety: Model F lmer(na ~ previous + students + juried + public + solo + mpqpem + mpqab + orch + mpqnem + mpqnem:solo + (previous + students + juried + public + solo | id), REML = T), the indicators recoded from audience (Instructor the reference), perform_type (solo vs ensembles) and instrument (orchestral vs voice and keyboard) as the chapter's mutate does; derived terms name their column once. diary is previous + 1, pa (positive affect) an alternate response. Models A to E share response and grouping.

formula: SYS ~ MNACT5 + STR + HAP + TIR + DAY + POSTURE + PHASE + AGE + FH123 + timepass + (1 | SNUM)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 (ch-lon) open-ended exercise 1, UCLA nurse blood pressure study (Goldstein et al. 2000, data from Weiss 2005): 40-60 readings per nurse (SNUM) over one day, systolic BP the primary response, asked for multilevel models relating work conditions (activity, mood, work status) to BP trends; no model fitted, the formula is proposed from the listed variables. Responses in page order: rows 2 and 3 are DIA and HRT, the alternatives the page names; it also suggests modeling the mood ratings, which here are covariates. timept indexes the reading; time (minutes from midnight) is left as an unused column.

formula: DIA ~ MNACT5 + STR + HAP + TIR + DAY + POSTURE + PHASE + AGE + FH123 + timepass + (1 | SNUM)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 open-ended exercise 1, diastolic BP, the first alternative response the page names; design and proposed model as row 1.

formula: HRT ~ MNACT5 + STR + HAP + TIR + DAY + POSTURE + PHASE + AGE + FH123 + timepass + (1 | SNUM)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 open-ended exercise 1, heart rate, the second alternative response the page names; design and proposed model as row 1.

formula: germin ~ species * (soil + sterile) + (1 | pot)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 2, Seed germination (Angell 2010): the wide table, one row per plant, with whether the seed germinated as the response, asked for multilevel GLMs of soil type and sterilization effects, separately for coneflowers and leadplants; no model fitted. Plants nest in pots, and soil, sterile and species are pot-level, so the separate analyses are rendered as species interactions with a pot intercept. RULE GAP: the heights hgt13 to hgt28 are repeated measures stored as columns (ch. 10's case study gathers them into a three-level long table, Models A to F by lmer), but the germination model the book poses reads the rows as stored, so the table is filed rather than excluded as wide; the heights are alternate responses, plant a row id.

formula: HEIGHT ~ I(YEAR - 1990) * TUBEX + (I(YEAR - 1990) || ID) + (I(YEAR - 1990) || TRANSECT)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 10 (ch-3level) guided exercise 1, Tree tubes (Eisinger et al. 2011): the long table, one row per tree and year, a three-level model for height with years within trees (ID) within transects; Model C is the unconditional growth model in TIME = YEAR - 1990 with uncorrelated random effects at levels two and three, and Model D adds the TUBEX by TIME interaction (TUBEX's main effect kept, as lme4's * writes it). Ch. 7 (ch-corrdata) fits lmer(growth_yr1 ~ tubes + (1|transect)) on first-year growth, the 1991 minus 1990 height of each tree, a pivot of two rows that no column holds, so it is no row. SPECIES is left as an unused column.

formula: stars_given ~ length + year + rev_count_user + rev_count_biz + (1 | user_id) + (1 | name)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 4, Yelp restaurant reviews in Madison (Mohr 2018): reviews of restaurants by reviewers, the page noting that user and restaurant can be crossed random effects; its first modeling idea is the number of stars (or whether it is 5), the others whether at least one person found the review useful (row 2) or cool (row 3). No model fitted, the covariates are proposed. The table has no restaurant id, so name is the restaurant factor (a chain's branches share it). avg_user_stars and avg_biz_stars average the response, text is free text, year_index repeats year, funny is an unused vote count.

formula: I(useful > 0) ~ stars_given + length + year + rev_count_user + rev_count_biz + (1 | user_id) + (1 | name)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 open-ended exercise 4, the second idea: whether at least one person thought the review useful, with user and restaurant crossed; design and proposal as row 1. RULE GAP: the documented response is the binary recode of the vote count useful, so response_type records what the column holds (count) while the formula keeps the source's recode.

formula: I(cool > 0) ~ stars_given + length + year + rev_count_user + rev_count_biz + (1 | user_id) + (1 | name)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 open-ended exercise 4, the third idea: whether at least one person thought the review cool; design and proposal as row 1. RULE GAP: the binary recode of the vote count cool, as row 2.

formula: QN66 ~ Q2 + bmipct + Q81 + (1 | stratum:psu)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 6 (ch-logreg), case study Reducing the risk of obesity: the 2009 Youth Risk Behavior Survey; the chapter's code reads this file, draws 500 students (set.seed(33)), recodes Q66 to lose.wt (trying to lose weight), Q2 to sex, Q84 to sport and Q81 to media hours, keeps complete cases and writes risk2009.csv, on which it fits glm(lose.wt.01 ~ female + bmipct + media, family = binomial) (model4; sport was dropped). QN66, the survey's own trying-to-lose-weight indicator, is that recode. The book treats students as independent; the survey's primary sampling unit psu (within stratum) is a cluster the rows repeat within, rendered as a random intercept, at low since no source fits it. weight is the survey weight; the book enters Q81 as numeric hours.

formula: I(1000 / rt) ~ 1 + nchar(as.character(item)) + (1 | item) + (1 | subj)
notes: Embrace Uncertainty (Alday, Kliegl and Bates), ch. Large-scale designed experiments (largescaledesigned.qmd at 08f020d7): English Lexicon Project lexical decision trials (Balota et al. 2007), subjects and items incompletely crossed; elm01 fits 1000 / rt ~ 1 + isword * wrdlen + (1 | item) + (1 | subj) on the trials with non-missing acc and 200 <= rt <= 3000 (elm02 also drops subjects under 80% accuracy); MixedModelsDatasets.jl docs/src/datasets.md (36eaaacb, sha256 equal to the pin) give the same model. RULE GAP: isword (word or nonword) and wrdlen are joined from ELP_ldt_item; wrdlen is the item's length, written as nchar(item), but isword and its interaction with wrdlen have no column in this table and are left out of the formula. seq is the trial number; acc is row 2's response.

formula: acc ~ 1 + nchar(as.character(item)) + (1 | item) + (1 | subj)
notes: Embrace Uncertainty, ch. Analysis of accuracy in the LDT (LDT_accuracy.qmd at 08f020d7): gm1 = fit(MixedModel, @formula(acc ~ 1 + isword * wrdlen + (1|item) + (1|subj)), trials, Bernoulli()) on the trial table joined to ELP_ldt_item; also in MixedModelsDatasets.jl's docs. RULE GAP: isword has no column here, as in row 1; wrdlen is written as nchar(item).

formula: resp ~ 1 + time + I(time^2):Group + (1 + time + I(time^2) | Subj)
notes: Embrace Uncertainty, ch. Longitudinal data (longitudinal.qmd at 08f020d7), section Longitudinal data with treatments: Box (1950) rat body weights over weeks in three treatment groups; bxm01 to bxm05 are compared and the chapter's closing note says to go with bxm03, resp ~ 1 + time + time^2 & Group + (1 + time + time^2 | Subj), Group acting only on the curvature. Polynomial terms name their column once, so time:Group stands for the time^2 by Group term. MixedModelsDatasets.jl's docs fit bxm04 (random time slope only) as their second example.

formula: dv ~ 1 + Group * A * B + (1 | Subj)
notes: SMLP2025 (RePsychLing, a5a3c495), contrasts_kwdyz11.qmd, section An Example for a complex example: Group between subjects, A (2 levels) and B (3 levels) within, 6 measures per subject; m6_cpx (1 + A + B | Subj), m6_zcp (zerocorr) and m6_ovi (1 | Subj) share the fixed part dv ~ 1 + Group*A*B (SeqDiffCoding), and the rendered page's likelihood-ratio test finds neither richer model better than m6_ovi, the LMM supported by the data, written here. The page does not say where the data come from.

formula: zScore ~ 1 + Test * I(age - 8.5) * Sex + (1 + Test + I(age - 8.5) + Sex | School) + (1 + Test | Child) + (1 + Test || Cohort)
notes: SMLP2025 fggk21.qmd (a5a3c495), section Fitting the published LMM m1: Fühner, Golle, Granacher and Kliegl (2021, Scientific Reports) fit zScore ~ 1 + Test * a1 * Sex + (1 + Test + a1 + Sex | School) + (1 + Test | Child) + zerocorr(1 + Test | Cohort), a1 = age - 8.5, zScore the score z-standardized within Test, Test in SeqDiffCoding; SMLP refits it on a stratified subsample of 1000 boys and 1000 girls, and MixedModelsDatasets.jl's docs give a reduced version. score is the raw form of zScore in units that differ by Test. Cohort (9 levels) is fitted as random by the source. In lme4, || on the factor Test does not fully remove the correlations.

formula: rt ~ 1 + CTR * cardinal * size + (1 + CTR + cardinal | Subj)
notes: SMLP2025 kkl15.qmd (a5a3c495): Kliegl, Kuschela and Laubrock (2015) visual-attention replication, reaction times by cue-target relation (CTR, SeqDiffCoding), rectangle orientation (cardinal) and target size (size, between subjects); after two reduction strategies the page keeps m_cpx = m_prm1, rt ~ 1 + CTR * cardinal * size + (1 + CTR + cardinal | Subj), on raw rt for compatibility with kwdyz11; MixedModelsDatasets.jl's docs list the maximal and a zerocorr version.

formula: log(rt) ~ 1 + CTR + (1 + CTR | Subj)
notes: SMLP2025 kwdyz11.qmd (a5a3c495): Kliegl, Wei, Dambacher, Yan and Zhou (2011) visual-attention experiment, m1 = log(rt) ~ 1 + CTR + (1 + CTR | Subj), log scale chosen by a Box-Cox check (the model the paper reported, later found singular); contrasts_kwdyz11.qmd refits rt ~ 1 + CTR + (1 + CTR | Subj) under several codings of CTR, and MixedModelsDatasets.jl's docs give both. Item and dir (rectangle orientation) are in no documented model.

formula: height ~ 1 + age + (1 + age | Subj)
notes: No chapter of Embrace Uncertainty loads it. MixedModelsDatasets.jl docs/src/datasets.md (36eaaacb), whose sha256 for oxboys equals the pin, fit height ~ 1 + age + (1 + age | Subj) (Pinheiro and Bates 2000), age standardized; occasion is the measurement occasion, a recoding of age. A copy of nlme's Oxboys.
